rule_name: Hedge Where the Character Could Not Know, Cut Filler Everywhere Else
why: "Actually" is on rule 28's named list of filler words to cut wherever they attach to nothing and soften a claim the narrator is entitled to make plainly.
suggestion: Cut the hedge: "which is where he starts paying attention."

why: The chapter otherwise spells every number out ("four days," "eleven seconds," "six hours," "two seconds"); a bare numeral here breaks that house style the same way rule 35's own example flags "at 4" as a numeral stray among spelled-out numbers.
suggestion: Spell it out to match: "at oh-three-forty" or "at twenty to four in the morning."

rule_name: Bury Scale Inside a Fast List, Deliberately
quote: the entire encounter takes under two seconds and it does not go his way at any point in it
why: The third contact, an extraordinary near-perfect ambush overturned in under two seconds, gets three full paragraphs of scene treatment (lines 116-122) while the two more ordinary contacts are compressed into one breathless list-sentence at line 113; rule 7 requires the reverse, extraordinary material buried in the list and ordinary material given scene-time.
suggestion: Fold the third contact into the same fast list as the first two ("...and the third is 0340 on night four, from behind, position and timing and surprise and ground all his, under two seconds, still doesn't go his way"), and give one of the earlier contacts the paragraph-level scene treatment instead.

rule_name: Subordinate Instead of Chaining With And / Then
quote: runs through the four days and gets to the third contact and stops on it
why: Three sequential actions (runs through, gets to, stops) are coordinated with two "and"s instead of subordination, giving the routine walk-through and the meaningful pause equal grammatical weight.
suggestion: Subordinate it: "runs through the four days before stopping on the third contact."

rule_name: Crutch Phrases That Have Stopped Meaning Anything
why: "For a while" is one of rule 27's explicitly named universal duration markers, used here with no real duration or image attached to the pause.
suggestion: Replace with a real image: "stops on it, flips back two pages of notes."

rule_name: The Nobody Construction, Don't Normalise by Reporting an Absent Reaction
why: Reports an absent collective reaction to stand in for the room's response, the exact construction rule 3 bans, near-identical to its own example "Nobody turns around."
suggestion: Give one specific reaction instead: "The major looks at the clipboard instead of at Sam."

rule_name: Telling After Showing, Don't Explain the Image You Just Rendered
quote: He is being completely sincere and it is obvious that he is being completely sincere
why: Sam's sincerity was already fully rendered through his detailed, self-incriminating critique in the preceding line; this sentence explains the image immediately after showing it, and repeats "completely sincere" twice in the same breath to make sure it landed.
suggestion: Cut the sentence and go straight to the consequence: "It goes upward anyway."

quote: which is the part that goes upward
why: A trailing "which is..." clause telling the reader how to read the preceding fact is the automatic-fail evaluative construction STYLE_RULES section 8 bans (Guide 2 checklist item 3: any "which is the/what/how" evaluation).
suggestion: Cut the clause; let a following beat carry the consequence: "It goes upward anyway."
